entities.span: The authenticated app's page inventory, navigation, post sign in destination and header
rejected_spans: the gap features 9, 11 and 12 were each about to invent on their own

entities.span: Must land before feature 9 starts;
it does not block feature 7
rejected_spans: whose done when clause needs no decided shell

entities.span: **Done when:** `/search`, `/profile` and `/applications` exist as real routes with only the first two in the signed in nav;
one header component renders its signed in variant from `(app)/layout.tsx` and its signed out variant from the marketing layout;
a user with no profile row lands on `/profile` and everyone else on `/`, with feature 14's later scoring gate layered on top rather than replacing it;
a deep link followed while signed out survives sign in and returns the visitor to it, rejecting anything that is not a single leading slash path;
the signed in shell needs no hamburger, drawer or tab bar at 320 pixels;
and a signed in visitor at `/` no longer sees a sign in invitation, without `/` reading the session.

Design it (spec): `/architect app shell & navigation` · done 2026-08-31, spec 0008 at **revision 5**. Two adversarial cross model rounds (Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5) plus a decision completeness pass, all findings applied

The spec amends this row's **Done when** wording in two places, and `/develop` records both against the row when the feature ships. First, "everyone else on `/`" becomes `/search`. Second, "its signed out variant from the marketing layout" becomes each marketing page composing it.
rejected_spans: because that wording predates the settled decision that `/` is the static marketing page
because a layout never learns the pathname and the row's phrasing assumed it could

entities.span: **Revision 5, 2026-08-31**, added after the build: AC-3a's signed in half carried the same defect revision 4 fixed on the marketing half, so composition is now per page on both sides, which also amends this row's third **Done when** clause, "one header component renders its signed in variant from `(app)/layout.tsx`", to each route under `(app)` composing it.

Build it: `/develop app shell & navigation` · done 2026-08-31 on `feat/app-shell-and-navigation`, seven code commits. All four gates green (lint, format, typecheck, `pnpm build`), 365 unit tests and 52 integration tests passing, and the whole thread driven in a real browser against the local stack.

**The `Done when` wording above is amended in three places, recorded here rather than edited into it**. Two were named by the spec: "everyone else on `/`" is `/search`, and "its signed out variant from the marketing layout" is each marketing page composing it. The third was found during this build: "renders its signed in variant from `(app)/layout.tsx`" is now each route under `(app)` composing it
rejected_spans: so the row still reads as it was written when the feature was scoped
because AC-3a and AC-5 cannot both hold

entities.span: The return path thread, end to end: the two shared modules and the validator, the proxy echoing the requested path as a header, the layout appending `?next=`, `/sign-in` carrying it, the Server Actions writing the cookie, the callback consuming and clearing it · **AC-5b**, **AC-6**, **AC-7**, **AC-7a**, **AC-8**, **AC-9**, **AC-10**, **AC-10a**, **AC-11** to **AC-16**, **AC-24a**. Starts by proving the one mechanic the spec marks inferred rather than verified.
rejected_spans: **That mechanic holds, measured rather than reasoned about on 2026-08-31**: the cookie a Server Action writes survives that action's redirect off site. Driven in Chromium against the local stack, the browser reached `accounts.google.com` still holding `jobhunt_return_path` for `localhost`, scoped to `/auth/callback`, `httpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, and the callback then read it, honoured it and cleared it, with a second callback carrying nothing. **The recorded fallback is not needed.** The proxy's half is locked by an integration test that fails when the headers are hoisted, checked by reintroducing that exact bug

entities.span: The door, the entry page swap and the sign in bounce: `/go` with `no-store`, `/` losing every provider form, and a signed in visitor at `/sign-in` bounced · **AC-17**, **AC-17a**, **AC-18**, **AC-19**, **AC-20**. `/` still builds as a static prerender, so its accepted contract holds. The band's opening clause "Sign in with Google or GitHub" was **deleted at the engineer's direction**
rejected_spans: since AC-18 asks for no sign in invitation anywhere and the spec's Copy table did not cover that sentence

entities.span: The shell itself: the chrome only header, the marketing pages composing their own variant, the three routes with their copy slots, `/health` tidied · **AC-1** to **AC-5a**, **AC-21**, **AC-22**, **AC-23**.
rejected_spans: **AC-4 failed on first measurement and is now fixed**: the 190 pixel lockup left 82 pixels at 320, so every route under the shell overflowed, and so did `/` and `/sign-in`, because the door's "Open JobHunt" is wider than the "Sign in" jump it replaced. The chrome now renders the mark below `sm` and the lockup above it, and all seven routes measure exactly 320 by 320

entities.span: The three span names registered in `docs/observability/spans.md` · **AC-24**

Verify it: `/check verify app shell & navigation` · **PASS** on 2026-08-31, all 24 acceptance criteria met and all 28 steps in [verify.md](../specs/0008-app-shell-and-navigation/verify.md) ticked with the observation that proved each one.
rejected_spans: Twenty seven were driven against the real local stack in Chromium; the real Google handshake was run by the engineer on the branch preview, which is the one step a local run cannot reach. Two criteria the build had listed as unprovable were proved here: **AC-7a**, by stopping PostgREST so the profile read genuinely errored, after which the user with no profile row landed on `/search` rather than `/profile`, and the keyboard pass through the signed in header. **AC-4 is the one worth re measuring on any later change**, since it failed first during the build and now sits at exactly 320 by 320 on all seven routes
entities.unclassified_note: A stage line that only reports a check already performed rather than delivering one.

entities.span: Test it: `/test app shell & navigation` · done 2026-08-31, **57 new tests across four files**, all green, suite now 422 unit and 52 integration.
rejected_spans: They cover the surfaces the build left proved only by a browser walk: the door at `/go`, the `/sign-in` bounce, the `/auth/callback` handler, and the four `(app)` call sites. **The last of those was raised independently twice**, by the gap analysis at the start of this run and by the cross check on spec 0008 revision 5, which noticed that `app-header.test.ts` hands the component its own props and so can never fail when a route passes the wrong `current`. Each file was checked for vacuousness against the real code: changing `/profile` to `current="search"` fails two tests, and removing the callback's cookie clear plus the door's `no-store` fails seven
